title: The たら and なら conditionals
summary: たら is the past form plus ら: "once that has happened". It alone can talk about the past. なら attaches to a noun or clause as "if it is the case that".

blocks.text: Conditionals often swap places, but each has its own flavor. Here are the last two.
たら: the past form + ら
Take any verb or adjective in its **past** form (た / だ / かった) and add **ら**. It means "once that is done". Because it builds on the past, it fits situations that are already fulfilled.

blocks.jp: 起きたら、雪が積もっていた。
blocks.en: When I got up, snow had piled up.

blocks.jp: 家に帰ったら、さくらがいた。
blocks.en: When I got home, Sakura was there.

blocks.text: In the past, たら is the only conditional you can use, and it means **"when"** and often carries **surprise**: plain て or から would be flat; an if-word says "I did not expect this".
For the future, たら stresses **what happens once the condition is met**, while ば stresses **whether it will be met at all**. When you expect the condition to happen, たら leans towards "when".

blocks.jp: 雨がやんだら、出かけよう。
blocks.en: Once the rain stops, let's go out.

blocks.text: A small っ gives **ったら** (and the stronger **ってば**): a shortened "when it comes to ..." with a tone of mild complaint, often teasing.

blocks.jp: お母さんったら、また忘れたの。

blocks.text: **なら** attaches directly to a noun or a full clause. It takes up what was said or is clearly the case: "if it's X (as you say / as it is)".

blocks.en: If it's Sakura, she can do it.
If you mean the station, it is over there.

items: **Past form + ら**: once that has happened; the only if-form for the past.
In the past, it can carry surprise.
**Noun or clause + なら**: if it is the case that; "since it's X".

questions.instruction: Pick the たら form of 食べる
Pick the たら form of 高い

questions.prompt: 家に帰ったら、さくらがいた。
options: When I got home, Sakura was (surprisingly) there
If I go home, Sakura will be there
questions.note: In the past, たら means "when" and implies surprise.

questions.instruction: Which conditional can talk about something already past?

options: If it's Sakura, she can do it (I trust her)
questions.note: なら: given that it's her.

questions.instruction: How does this answer the question?
questions.prompt: 「駅はどこですか。」「駅なら、あそこです。」
options: If you mean the station, it is over there
I do not know the station
questions.note: なら picks up the topic that was just raised.

questions.prompt: 日本人＿＿、知っているよ。 (If he is Japanese, he knows.)
questions.note: なら attaches straight to a noun.

questions.prompt: たら stresses what happens once the condition is met; ば stresses whether it will be met.
questions.note: That is the difference in feel.

questions.prompt: Once the rain stops, let's go out.

questions.instruction: In which sentence does たら mean "when" (already happened)?
options: 起きたら、雪が積もっていた
questions.note: The past tense of the main clause shows it already happened.
